title: Human-capital formation is shaped by homes, neighborhoods, and workplaces as learning progress stalls and opportunity remains place-dependent
source_unit: World Bank, Human Capital Report 2026: Building Human Capital Where It Matters
geography: Global and cross-country evidence on health, learning, skills, employment, homes, neighborhoods, and workplaces

progress_direction.value: progress in building human capital has slowed and in many places declined

learning_trend.value: student learning showed limited progress over the last 15 years in low- and lower-middle-income countries, with most doing worse than in 2010

economic_channel.value: weak learning outcomes limit productivity, lifetime earnings, and economic growth

observations.method: World Bank cross-country human-capital evidence combining health, education, employment, and learning indicators.
observations.uncertainty: The report synthesizes country and population evidence; it is not a respondent-level longitudinal dataset and does not identify one causal explanation for every country trend.
observations.subgroup: Children and youth in low- and lower-middle-income countries, workers, families, schools, health systems, and policymakers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stalled global progress can be reversed through targeted investment in the settings where skills and health are actually formed.

denominator.unit: children and family human-capital formation frame

maternal_education_gradient.value: children whose mothers have more education perform better on vocabulary and mathematics tests

care_mechanism.value: nurturing, reading, play, emotional support, and safety contribute to skill development beyond material resources

adult_earnings_channel.value: the report cites evidence that supportive interventions can improve adult earnings by nearly 40 percent

policy_route.value: cash transfers, job programs, and tools for stimulating home environments can support family resources and care

observations.method: Review and synthesis of cross-country evidence on family resources, parental education, care, learning, and later-life outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The reported association and intervention evidence do not mean every household receives the same benefit; family structure, implementation, selection, and local services matter.
observations.subgroup: Children, adolescents, parents, mothers, low-resource families, caregivers, and households receiving income or employment support.
observations.counterinterpretation: Material resources and care are complements rather than substitutes; policy can expand both without treating families as interchangeable production units.

denominator.unit: neighborhood opportunity and human-capital comparison frame

income_same_different_outcomes.value: families with the same income can have very different outcomes depending on where they live

brazil_earnings_difference.unit: approximate share of earnings for a low-income child in a low-income Brazilian neighborhood relative to a low-income child in a high-income neighborhood

neighborhood_channels.value: schools, clinics, safety, pollution, streets, and job access jointly shape learning, health, and opportunity

coordination_need.value: education, environment, health, and infrastructure policy may need to work together to realize human-capital gains

observations.method: Place-based comparative evidence linking neighborhood conditions with human-capital and earnings outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: Neighborhood comparisons may reflect selection, local institutions, environmental conditions, and unmeasured family differences; the result is not a universal causal coefficient.
observations.subgroup: Low-income children, families in disadvantaged neighborhoods, residents exposed to violence or pollution, and communities with weak service access.
observations.counterinterpretation: Neighborhood disadvantage can be reduced through coordinated service quality, environmental improvement, safe mobility, and access to jobs rather than treated as a fixed social characteristic.

denominator.unit: workers and workplace learning opportunity frame in low- and middle-income countries

informal_or_small_scale_work.unit: approximate share of workers in low- and middle-income countries in small-scale agriculture, low-quality self-employment, or micro firms

experience_returns.value: earnings for self-employed workers increase only about half as much with the same gain in experience as for salaried workers

learning_constraint.value: many workers are in jobs with limited on-the-job learning opportunities

policy_route.value: employer training, apprenticeships, job matching, childcare, and safe commutes can make work more supportive of learning and participation

observations.method: Cross-country labor-market and human-capital synthesis focused on workplace learning, job type, experience, and participation.
observations.uncertainty: Occupational categories and earnings comparisons conceal heterogeneity in firm quality, sector, hours, selection, and informal work; they are not individual employment histories.
observations.subgroup: Self-employed workers, micro-firm workers, agricultural workers, labor-market entrants, women, caregivers, employers, and apprentices.
observations.counterinterpretation: Informal and small-scale work can build skills when linked to training, networks, technology, and markets; the report identifies constraints, not inevitable low productivity.

related_sources.claim: The World Bank Human Capital Data Portal provides complementary HCI+ country comparisons and methodology.
The World Bank Open Knowledge Repository provides the full report and chapter materials.

boundary: This record adds a human-capital route across homes, care, neighborhoods, learning, workplaces, informal work, gender participation, and place-based opportunity. It uses World Bank aggregate comparisons and report synthesis, not respondent-level data, individual child development histories, household time diaries, individual employment panels, causal neighborhood estimates, or proof that a policy works identically across settings.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official World Bank Human Capital Report 2026 page reviewed for the title, stalled learning progress, home and care mechanisms, neighborhood opportunity, workplace learning, 70 percent work composition estimate, and HCI+ framing.
